en.headline: Retired executive loses over HK$6 million in pickleball group investment scam
en.dek: Police said a former telecommunications senior manager was contacted via a sports platform pickleball group and transferred funds to a fake investment site for crypto and oil.
body: Police said a retired local man who previously held a senior management role at a telecommunications company lost more than HK$6 million after fraudsters approached him through a pickleball group on the sports social platform ReClub.

According to the force's CyberDefender account, the victim received a private message from someone posing as a fellow racket-sports enthusiast. After building trust through conversation about the sport, the person recommended cryptocurrency and crude oil investments that promised high returns.

The fraudsters then sent a link to a fake investment website. The man registered and, following instructions from purported customer service staff, made multiple transfers to unidentified Faster Payment System accounts and personal bank accounts. When he tried to withdraw the funds, the site demanded a deposit and administrative fees, after which he transferred more money before realising the deception.

Police said they had received more than 40 reports of online investment scams in the past week, with total losses exceeding HK$50 million. Officers reminded the public to be wary of unsolicited messages on any platform, to avoid unknown links, and to treat high-return investment pitches with caution, especially when transfers are requested to personal accounts.

zh.headline: 退休電訊高層墮匹克球群組投資騙局損失逾600萬元
zh.dek: 警方指事主在運動平台匹克球群組被私訊搭詔，誤信高回報加密貨幣及原油投資後轉賬至假網站，最終無法提款。
body: 警方表示，一名曾擔任電訊公司高層管理人員的本地退休男子，透過運動社群平台ReClub的匹克球群組接獲私訊後，墮入網上投資騙局，損失超過600萬港元。
警方在「CyberDefender守網者」專頁指出，騙徒冒充球類運動愛好者與事主交流打球心得，建立信任後推介加密貨幣及原油等聲稱可獲高回報的投資產品。
其後騙徒向事主發送虛假投資網站連結。事主登記後按假客服指示，多次轉賬至不明轉數快及個人銀行戶口。當他要求提款時，對方再要求繳交保證金及行政費，事主再次轉賬後才發現受騙。
警方指過去一周共接獲逾40宗網上投資騙案，總損失超過5000萬港元。警方提醒市民提防任何平台的陌生私訊，切勿點擊不明連結，並對高回報投資推介保持警惕，尤其涉及轉賬至個人戶口的情況。
